title: A real Repo Audit engine: Repository Intelligence
description: Owner direction 2026-10-21: rebuild a proper, professional repo audit engine. Found: the Builder's Repo Audit calls /api/audit/*, which the Runtime does not serve, so it always falls back to simulated progress (random timers) and a hard-coded sample report (invented advisories for axios and ws), and its fix plan and diffs are mocked helpers. The Runtime has a small real audit (apps/lumina-runtime/src/audit, 435 lines, /api/runtime/audit) and framework detection (63 lines) that the Builder does not use, and a RepositoryManifest type and analyzer under knowledge/repository. This violates the charter's No Mock Production Logic. The workspace's visual rebuild is MS-2026-0011's Repo Audit task and builds on this engine.
objective: Repo Audit reports real, evidence-backed, deterministic findings for any imported repository, from a Runtime engine that also produces its Repository Manifest (Release Plan V1 Milestone 2).
risks: The engine reads imported repositories only inside their project workspace and never sends their code or secrets anywhere.
Deep mode runs the project's own scripts; it runs only on the owner's request, inside the project's isolated workspace.
Security advisories need the network; offline, the report must say advisories were not checked rather than show none.

tasks.title: Repository inventory and Repository Manifest
acceptanceCriteria: Files, languages, package manager, workspaces, frameworks and entry points are recorded in a Repository Manifest for every audited project
The same repository at the same commit produces the same manifest
Manifests are kept per project with history

tasks.title: Dependency analysis
acceptanceCriteria: Imported but undeclared, declared but unused, and lockfile mismatches are found from the code itself
Every finding names the file and line or the package.json entry

tasks.title: Security analysis from real sources
acceptanceCriteria: Advisories come from the package manager's own audit; when it cannot run, the report says so instead of inventing any
Secrets in tracked files are reported by file and line, never by value
Risky code patterns are reported with file and line

tasks.title: Build health
acceptanceCriteria: Deep mode runs the project's typecheck and build in its isolated workspace
Errors are reported with file, line and message

tasks.title: Environment analysis
acceptanceCriteria: Variables the code reads are compared with what the project declares
Missing and unused variables are listed by name only

tasks.title: Architecture map
acceptanceCriteria: Module graph, entry points, import cycles and files no entry point reaches

tasks.title: Scoring and report
acceptanceCriteria: Per-category and overall scores derived only from findings
Every finding has a stable ID and its evidence
Two runs on the same commit give identical reports

tasks.title: Runtime audit API with live progress
acceptanceCriteria: Start, stream progress, read the latest report and history per project
Fix plans are built only from real findings through the existing fix registry

tasks.title: Repo Audit reads only the Runtime engine
acceptanceCriteria: Simulated progress, the sample report and the mocked fix helpers are removed
The PDF export uses the real report
When Runtime is unreachable, the workspace says so instead of showing sample data

validationPlan: Audit of the KoreLumina repository and of a small sample repository: findings checked by hand against the code
Two runs on the same commit produce identical reports
